voyage.content: Kam Shan Country Park, also known as Monkey Hill, is famous for its wild monkeys. It is at the north of Kowloon and so can be easily accessed by taking the KMB route 72 or 81 from Kowloon or New Territories. A free barbecue site is available in the country park.

voyage.name: New Town Plaza
voyage.address: 17-18 Sha Tin Centre St, Sha Tin
voyage.content: This is a huge shopping complex in Sha Tin which sells mid-range goods of all types. Well worth a visit but it will be crowded on weekends. Accessible through the Shatin MTR station, change at Kowloon Tong or Hung Hom station if travelling from Kowloon and Admiralty station if travelling from Hong Kong island. It also connects with a few nearby but smaller shopping malls via the footbridge networks.

voyage.name: Ma On Shan Plaza
voyage.address: Ma On Shan Plaza, 608 Sai Sha Rd, Ma On Shan, Hong Kong
voyage.content: A large shopping plaza in Ma On Shan with a variety of stores. The items are more affordable as the plaza is located in a less-affluent area. It has a series of footbridges that connect to other shopping complexes such as Sunshine City Plaza and MOSTown. Accessible through Ma On Shan MTR station, change at Tai Wai or Diamond Hill if travelling from Kowloon and Hong Kong Island.

voyage.name: Tai Po Megamall
voyage.address: No.8 & 10 On Pong Road, Tai Po
voyage.content: A group of shopping malls in the district. It is less crowded than New Town Plaza. Easily accessible by MTR and KMB buses. Take bus K12 from Tai Po Market Railway Station. It can also be reached by the buses which terminates at Tai Po Central.

voyage.name: Tai Wo Shopping Mall
voyage.content: It is next to Tai Wo Station is a typical shopping centre in a public housing estate. Do not expect a variety choice of shops are available, but goods are at reasonable price because the target customers are local people.

voyage.name: Hang Heung (zh 恒香)
voyage.content: It is arguably Hong Kong's most famous Chinese bakery and famous among ethnic Chinese worldwide for its wife cakes (老婆餅). Other products include egg rolls (蛋卷) and almond biscuits (杏仁餅).

voyage.name: Uptown Plaza
voyage.content: Next to Tai Po Market Railway Station is a regional shopping centre in Tai Po.

voyage.name: Wo Sang
voyage.content: Next to Kei Lun Light rail station in Tuen Mun. It is famous for its traditional Hong Kong dishes. You can sit next to the kitchen and watch how they cook the fried dishes. The roast goose here is also famous.

voyage.name: Learn Hop
voyage.content: Next to the Siu Hong MTR station. Located inside the Siu Hong Commercial Complex. It is famous for its choice of Guangdong, wonton and dumpling noodles. Also serves Zha jiang mian.

voyage.name: Tai Po Hui Market
voyage.content: A modern complex of small stalls. The must-try items are fried pork chop noodles and fish ball noodles. Also, for as little as $10 a dish, you can choose from a variety of culinary styles, including local favourites and dishes from Shanghai, Japan and south Asia. Tai Po Hui Market cooked food centre is located near Tai Po Market MTR Station.

voyage.name: Chan Kun Kee
voyage.content: Wo Che Estate, Sha Tin. A typical Dai Pai Dong in Hong Kong providing a variety of Cantonese dishes. Get off at Sha Tin Railway Station and take a taxi to Wo Che Estate.

voyage.name: Cheung Wah Estate
voyage.content: Cooked Food Centre near Fanling MTR Station. It is a cooked food centre located in a public housing estate. Dishes start at $10 up.

voyage.name: Pai Tau Restaurant
voyage.content: Pai Tau Rd, Sha Tin. This little eatery in a stretch of old shophouses near MTR Sha Tin offers basic Cantonese fare with lunch sets for around $25. No English menu, but the staff are happy to assist.

voyage.name: Ho To Tai dumpling wonton noodle
voyage.address: G/F, no.67, On Ning Road, Yuen Long

voyage.name: Fu Ah Seafood Restaurant
voyage.address: G/F 27, Hoi Pong St, Sai Kung
voyage.content: The second-to-last in Sai Kung's seafood restaurant alley, this unassuming joint does good set meals for $150/person, with reasonably priced beer and no surprises in the bill.

voyage.name: Dragon Inn Seafood Restaurant
voyage.address: 19.5 Miles, Castle Peak Road, Tuen Mun
voyage.content: is a famous seafood restaurant in Tuen Mun. The price is more valuable than Sai Kung and you can go to the Sam Shing market to choose your seafood which would provide more variation. It is ranked one of the best seafood restaurant in Hong Kong.

voyage.name: Shanghai Po Po
voyage.address: Shop 3207, Phase 1, Tuen Mun Town Plaza, 3 Tuen Lung Street, Tuen Mun
voyage.content: One of the best chain restaurant to eat the Shanghainese food. It serves big dishes at a value price. It's famous for its dan dan noodles and hot and sour soup.

voyage.name: Lung Wah Hotel
voyage.content: It is famous for roasted pigeons.

voyage.name: Bradbury Jockey Club Youth Hostel
voyage.alt: 白普理賽馬會青年旅舍
voyage.content: A youth hostel in Tai Po. Lots of boating, walking and cycling opportunities nearby and right by the scenic Plover Cove Reservoir.

voyage.name: Ascension House
voyage.address: 33 Tao Fong Shan Rd, Sha Tin
voyage.content: A hostel run by a Christian group near Shatin. Located in the “jungle” on a mountain in the New Territories, they provide three meals a day including laundry, and have friendly, amiable staff on site.

voyage.name: Panda Hotel
voyage.content: Tsuen Wan. With over 1,026-rooms, you're sure to find one that takes your fancy. Keep in shape by working out at the gym, or take a dip in their huge outdoor pool.

voyage.name: Royal View Hotel
voyage.content: Tsuen Wan. Uniquely situated amongst between the Ting Kau and Lido beaches, all 691 rooms give a superb view of the sea. Furnished in a modern design, all rooms feature a kitchen and are fitted out in the latest accessories.

voyage.name: Harbour Plaza Resort City
voyage.address: 18 Tin Yan Rd, Tin Shui Wai
voyage.content: Has rooms and serviced suites, most of which overlook the Tin Shui Wai Central Park. The only hotel in Tin Shui Wai.

voyage.name: Hyatt Regency Sha Tin
voyage.content: Opened in 2009, this is the first Western-branded hotel in the New Territories, and not only is it gorgeous, but costs about a third of the price of an equivalent hotel in Kowloon or the Island. Facilities include spa, heated pool, popular restaurant, apartments for long stays. The downside is the location: it's not even in central Sha Tin, but two stops out by MTR, at least 20 min from the city and with virtually no

voyage.name: Regal Riverside
voyage.content: Tai Chung Kiu Road Shatin. Four-star hotel overlooking the stunning Shing Mun River. The hotel offers a range of facilities and services including airport transfers, jacuzzis and car rental services for convenience and comfort.

voyage.name: Royal Park Hotel
voyage.address: 8 Pak Hok Ting St, Sha Tin
voyage.content: Four-star hotel conveniently located adjacent to New Town Plaza and with easy access to Sha Tin MTR station. Connected by a covered bridge, lots of amenities such as restaurants, department store, book store, supermarket and even a movie theatre are found in the malls nearby. It has a nice view overlooking the Shing Mun River.

voyage.name: Cheung Chau
voyage.content: A traditional community based on an active fishing fleet and many thriving seafood restaurants. It has a number of reasonable hiking trails and some usable beaches.

voyage.name: Peng Chau
voyage.content: Although it has a reputation for being dull and lacking in tourist attractions, you may be nevertheless be pleasantly surprised. Restaurants here are cheaper than the other islands and you get the feeling you are off the 'beaten-track' of mass tourism. Perhaps it is the place to go at the end of your holiday when you are weary of the fast-pace of the big city and just want to slow down, have a drink and chat with fri

voyage.name: Lamma Island
voyage.content: Has become increasingly popular with Western hippies who have created their own small residential community in Yung Shue Wan (榕樹灣). On both sides of the island you will find attractive bars, restaurants and cafes, making it a popular destination for local Chinese people out on a day trip.

voyage.name: Po Toi islands
voyage.content: Around 3km south of Hong Kong island. The Po Toi Islands are about six small island where only Po Toi Island is inhabited. However, during the fishing season there may be around six thousand people living around the islands. The most famous seafood on Po Toi are octopus and "Ma You" Fish (馬鮪魚). Go to Po Toi Island to see the famous rock formations and eat good seafood. You are advised to reserve tables at the restaur

voyage.name: Soko islands
voyage.content: Found in the southwest of the Hong Kong SAR. They comprise seven small islands and nine sets of reefs. Today, these islands are uninhabited but in the distant past they were home to many people.

voyage.name: Tap Mun Chau
voyage.content: Also known as Grass Island, is in the North East of the territory. It has about 100 residents, mostly fishermen. Its main attraction is its isolation and quality seafood restaurant that was made famous by the patronage of Hong Kong's last governor, Chris Patten.

voyage.name: Tung Lung Chau
voyage.content: Meaning 'east dragon island' in Cantonese, it is found off Clearwater Bay. It has another name: 'Nam Tong island' (南堂島).

voyage.name: Tung Ping Chau
voyage.content: Found in the North East of Hong Kong, in Mirs Bay (大鵬灣). Today, Tung Ping Chau does not have many residents, however, it used to be a very important island during the war between Japan and China. Then it was an important underground transport route between China and Hong Kong. It was also used by the British military and others who were fighting against Japan. In its heyday, there were 10 villages, providing accommod

voyage.name: Waglan island
voyage.content: Near Po Toi, is famous for its lighthouse.

voyage.name: Kwo Chau islands
voyage.content: Located to the east of Hong Kong island. There are three main islands and 29 small islands. The Kwo Chau Islands look like a bowl of fruit from the air and so this is how they got their name. Likewise, the three main islands look like nine pins from the sky, hence the name. Individually, they are known as East Ninepin Island (Tung Kwo Chau), South Ninepin Island (Nam Kwo Chau) and North Ninepin Island (Pak Kwo Chau).

voyage.name: Hong Kong Disneyland
voyage.content: Asia's second Disneyland was opened in September 2005 and features some of the Disney favourites. The park is accessible via the MTR. Change at the Sunny Bay station on the Tung Chung MTR line for the Disneyland Resort Line. It has nine themed areas: Main Street USA, Adventureland, Fantasyland, Tomorrowland, Toy Story Land, Grizzly Gulch, Mystic Point, World of Frozen and Stark Expo. Tickets are $639 for adults, $475

voyage.name: Inspiration Lake Recreation Centre
voyage.content: Inspiration Lake is the largest artificial lake in Hong Kong, and has a 1500-m jogging trail. It also has an arboretum, and rents paddle boats and surrey bikes. It is in Penny's Bay, a 15-minute walk from Disneyland Resort MTR station, or take the R8 bus.

voyage.name: Ngong Ping 360
voyage.content: A spectacular 5.7-km cable car journey that takes in an impressive cultural themed village and the Tian Tan Buddha. At the themed village there are a couple of attractions. The Walking with Buddha attraction gives an interesting introduction to Buddha, and has different stages, with headphones giving the narration in a variety of languages. The Monkey's Tail is simply a silent animated movie, with a simple moral. A l

voyage.name: Tian Tan Buddha
voyage.content: At over 250 tonnes and 34 m in height, this was the largest seated outdoor bronze Buddha statue in the world, until the statue of Dordenna Buddha near Thimphu in Bhutan was finished in 2015. The site also offers unobstructed views over the island. Access to the Buddha is free, although entering the museum inside during busy times requires a meal ticket for the vegetarian restaurant; a snack costs $23 while full meals

voyage.name: Po Lin Monastery
voyage.content: The monastery was founded in 1906 by three monks from Jiangsu province. The main temple building houses three bronze statues representing the Buddha of the past, present and future.

voyage.name: Tai O
voyage.content: A traditional fishing village with houses built on stilts over the sea. Tai O also called "Eastern Venice".

voyage.name: Discovery Bay
voyage.content: As a residential district, Discovery Bay is not really a tourist destination. However, it boasts a 400-m beach, a golf and marina club for members and guests, meaning that the area attracts day trippers. It also holds festivals, including most notably, dragon boat races at the beach in May/June and a multicultural festival in November.

voyage.name: Mui Wo
voyage.alt: traditional Chinese: 梅窩, Pinyin: Méiwō, lit. "plum nest"
voyage.content: a rural town on the eastern coast of Lantau Island. The main beach in Mui Wo is known as Silver Mine Bay (銀礦灣). There are fast and slow ferry services from Central to Mui Wo. Central - Mui Wo Ferry The fast ferry costs $25 and takes 30 minutes. The slow ferry costs $15, takes 50 minutes and you can go outside. The 3M bus takes you from Tung Chung to Mui Wo. There are a number of temples and old buildings. There is al

voyage.name: Lantau Peak
voyage.content: At 934 m, the second highest point in Hong Kong and the highest point on Lantau Island. You can also stay overnight at the Ngong Ping hostel, and wake up very early to reach the summit in time for the spectacular sunrise. Although not particularly high by international standards, this is a fairly hard climb and you should make full preparations, especially during summer.

voyage.name: The Stoep
voyage.content: Beachside restaurant with a good western menu and also specializes in serving South African dishes. Although the food is not the main attraction, the location of this restaurant makes it one of the best places to eat and drink in Hong Kong. Booking a table is advisable at weekends and Public Holidays.

voyage.name: High Tide Restaurant
voyage.content: Authentic Thai restaurant. Located right on the beach front, you might think you're in Thailand. An ideal place to get refreshments after a lazy day on one of Hong Kong's best beaches.

voyage.name: China Beach Club
voyage.content: Silvermine Bay (Mui Wo). Head for the beach in the bay and then carry on walking. Serves great food and drinks to the colonial crowd and locals alike. This is a doggie paradise in Hong Kong.

voyage.name: The China Bear
voyage.content: Mui Wo. Walk off the ferry and turn left and you will see a cafe/bar next to the sea. If you are looking for a "full English" breakfast, or some western beer, then you have found the right place.

voyage.name: Deli France
voyage.content: Near the MTR.

voyage.name: Pizza Hut
voyage.content: Near the MTR.

voyage.name: Food Republic
voyage.content: A large food court that is incredibly busy at lunch and dinner times on weekends with a lot of mainlanders hungry after a hard day of shopping.

voyage.name: Olea
voyage.content: With floor-to-ceiling glass windows of 7 m looking out to a man-made water and bamboo feature. Olea is a casual fine dining restaurant in the hotel and features an open Mediterranean kitchen, with a pizza oven and an array of various classic tapas and mezze dishes.

voyage.name: Essence
voyage.content: Located on the lobby level, Essence was designed by a world famous interior designer Yasumichi Morita.It is the main dining venue in the hotel and features international cuisine through buffet and à la carte offerings.

voyage.name: 360 Forest Grill & Restaurant Bar
voyage.content: Overlooking the cable car, 360 Forest Grill & Restaurant Bar offers alfresco dining in a peaceful, garden setting; only moments away from the hustle of Tung Chung. A wide range of a-la-cart grilled meats and fresh sea foods, three course buffet sets, and standard Asian and European dishes.

voyage.name: Hemingway’s by the Bay
voyage.content: Beachside dining with 80 indoor seats, 86 outside.

voyage.name: China Bear
voyage.address: G/F, Mui Wo Ctr, Mui Wo

voyage.name: Mcsorley's Ale House
voyage.address: Shop G11A, G/F, D Deck, Discovery Bay

voyage.name: Starz
voyage.content: There are few bar options in Tung Chung, and this is probably the best you are going to find.

voyage.name: Novotel Citygate Hong Kong
voyage.content: Novotel Citygate Hong Kong is 5 minutes from Hong Kong International Airport with free shuttle service. With direct access to mass transit railway (MTR), it takes 28 minutes to the city centre and Hong Kong Disneyland is 2 stops away.

voyage.name: Silver Mine Bay Hotel
voyage.content: Swimming pool, sauna, beach side. Breakfast included. 128 room hotel and resort.

voyage.name: Ngong Ping SG Davis Hostel at the Po Lin Monastery
voyage.content: Reservations made are not always acknowledged upon arrival, but sometimes when you're told they're booked solid you can still get a bunk. You needed to be a member of a Youth Hostel Association in order to get the best rates. Membership is available online.
